name: aar-multi-benchmark-paired-grounding-v3
goal: Review and register the user-provided sycophancy, MASK, AbstentionBench, and MiniCheck/LLM-AggreFact papers as provenance-tracked concept sources; co-author original paired alignment grounding and explicitly distinguish active coverage from supporting references.
intended_use: Grounding for a future AAR supervised-fine-tuning recipe whose challenge signal compares target behavior under neutral and pressure prompts.
source_constraints: Stage each reviewed local PDF and its concept summary separately under grounding/, with stable source IDs, upstream origin, and SHA-256 content provenance.
Use papers only to derive behavioral concepts, coverage requirements, and original scenario specifications; do not import benchmark datasets or evaluation items.
Do not copy or closely paraphrase prompts, examples, questions, answer choices, passages, or evaluation items from any paper or its referenced datasets.
Record each family's contributing sources and whether the paper supplies a primary behavior taxonomy or a cross-cutting design/quality constraint.
Do not equate document support, factual accuracy, honesty, sycophancy, and calibrated abstention, or claim that custom paired tasks reproduce the papers' original protocols.
Do not use AAR held-out evaluation data, benchmark mirrors, or benchmark names inside generated examples.
Keep underlying scenario facts, task intent, and truth conditions fixed within each neutral-versus-pressure pair.
Keep grounding and task partitions fixed during later meta-optimization; only declared pipeline mutable paths may change.
Re-review expanded grounding before changing the pipeline rubric or starting execution; earlier single-paper approval does not approve this revision.
